headline: Not yet. But Korea’s chip crack is spreading to Europe and US futures.
summary: After the Kospi's 5.46% fall on Tuesday 13 October, Nasdaq futures lost about 1%, European chipmakers opened lower and BlackRock cut US stocks to neutral. Intel and Broadcom's CEOs say capital is now AI's biggest constraint. CPI lands Wednesday.

analysis: The selloff that began in Seoul on Tuesday 13 October did not stay there. The Kospi closed at 6,035.35, down 5.46%, Samsung Electronics lost 7.39% and SK hynix 10.09%, and foreign investors sold a net 2.2 trillion won; the index is about a quarter below its July highs, on its longest losing streak in over two years. [1][2] Kioxia fell as much as 13.3% and SoftBank Group 8.5% in Tokyo, European chipmakers such as STMicroelectronics and ASML opened lower, and Nasdaq futures were down about 1%. [3][4]

Money is turning cautious. BlackRock’s Investment Institute ended its long-held overweight on US stocks on Monday 12 October, moving to neutral to manage volatility around the AI buildout, and went overweight short-dated Treasuries for the first time in six years. [7] In Singapore that day, Broadcom’s Hock Tan said capital might be AI’s biggest constraint and likened some investors to a casino; Intel’s Lip-Bu Tan called the cost of capital the main challenge. [6] SoftBank is paying up to 9.75% on new debt. [2]

Rates stay the trigger. The 10-year Treasury ended Friday 9 October at 5.24%, off a 5.365% high on 7 October; September CPI lands Wednesday 14 October, headline expected near 3.7%, with a December Fed hike priced near 90%. [4][5] Nvidia-backed Firmus scrapped a $5 billion Australian IPO on 9 October as investors balked at a $30.6 billion valuation and $30 billion of debt. [8] Why 77: the crack is spreading across regions and into futures, but no index has broken, so the score edges up in Critical. [2][4]
